hindi: देव सविता की प्रेरणा में, अश्विनों की भुजाओं से और पूषा के हाथों से मैं तुम्हें ग्रहण करता हूँ। तुम नारी हो; यहाँ मैं राक्षसों की गर्दनें काटता हूँ। तुम यव हो; हमसे द्वेषों को दूर करो, शत्रु-शक्तियों को दूर करो। द्युलोक के लिए तुम्हें, अन्तरिक्ष के लिए तुम्हें, पृथ्वी के लिए तुम्हें। पितरों के आसन वाले लोक शुद्ध हों। तुम पितरों का आसन हो।
english: At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the two Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take you. You are a woman; here I cut off the necks of the demons. You are barley; keep hatreds away from us, keep hostile powers away. You for heaven, you for the atmosphere, you for the earth. May the worlds, the seats of the fathers, be purified. You are the seat of the fathers.
notes: Unit holds three printed lines; kept as given. 'nāryasīdamaham' read as nārī asi idam aham; the line does not say who or what is addressed as 'woman'. The object of 'I take' is only tvā 'you'.

hindi: तुम अग्रगामी हो; हे सुगम प्रवेश वाले, उन्नेताओं के इस विषय में सावधान रहो। तुम पर कोई खड़ा होगा। देव सविता तुम्हें मधु से अभिषिक्त करें, उत्तम फल वाली ओषधियों के लिए तुम्हें। तुमने अग्र भाग से द्युलोक को छुआ, मध्य भाग से अन्तरिक्ष को भर दिया, निचले भाग से पृथ्वी को दृढ़ किया।
english: You are the leader; O you of good entry, take note of this of the unnetṛs. One will stand upon you. May the god Savitṛ anoint you with honey, you for the plants with good fruit. With your tip you touched heaven, with your middle you filled the atmosphere, with your lower part you made the earth firm.
notes: Obscure: 'svāveśa' taken as vocative 'of good entry' (could be nominative); 'vittāt' as imperative 'know'; 'supippalābhyaḥ' as 'good-fruited' (not identified as a plant). The subject of 'sthāsyati' is not stated. Who is addressed as tvā is not stated.

hindi: तुम्हारे जिन निवासों को हम पाना चाहते हैं, जहाँ बहुत सींगों वाली फुर्तीली गायें हैं, वहाँ उरुगाय विष्णु का वह परम पद निश्चय ही भरपूर नीचे लाया गया है। हे ब्रह्म को जीतने वाली, क्षत्र को जीतने वाली, धन और पुष्टि को जीतने वाली, मैं तुम्हें चारों ओर रखता हूँ। ब्रह्म को दृढ़ करो, क्षत्र को दृढ़ करो, आयु को दृढ़ करो, प्रजा को दृढ़ करो।
english: Those abodes of yours that we desire to reach, where the many-horned nimble cows are: there indeed the highest step of wide-striding Viṣṇu has been abundantly borne down. O you who win priestly power, who win ruling power, who win wealth and prosperity, I place you around. Make firm the priestly power, make firm the ruling power, make firm life, make firm offspring.
notes: Obscure: 'ayāsaḥ' glossed 'nimble' (doubtful); 'bhāri' is the printed form (the Ṛgveda parallel has 'bhāti'); not changed, rendered 'has been borne down'. 'brahmavani' etc. taken as vocatives addressed to tvā (case uncertain); 'brahma' as priestly power. 'paryūhāmi' translated 'I place around'.

hindi: विष्णु के कर्मों को देखो, जिनसे उसने व्रतों को देखा, जो इन्द्र का उपयुक्त मित्र है।
english: Look at the rites of Viṣṇu, from which he has beheld the ordinances, Indra's fitting friend.
notes: 'paspaśe' taken as 3 sg. perfect of √spaś 'behold'; the subject is not stated beyond 'friend of Indra'.

hindi: विष्णु के उस परम पद को ज्ञानी सदा देखते हैं, आकाश में फैली हुई आँख के समान।
english: The wise ones always see that highest step of Viṣṇu, like an eye spread out in the sky.
notes: Token '|di̱vī̱va̱' carries a stray bar attached; kept as given.

hindi: तुम घेरने वाले हो। दैवी प्रजाएँ तुम्हें चारों ओर से लपेट लें, इस यजमान को मनुष्यों के धन चारों ओर से घेर लें। तुम द्युलोक के पुत्र हो। पृथ्वी पर यह तुम्हारा लोक है। जंगली पशु तुम्हारा पशु है।
english: You are the encircler. May the divine clans wrap around you, and around this sacrificer the riches of men. You are the son of heaven. This is your world on the earth. The wild animal is your animal.

text_flags.why: stray Latin letter j after the word (probably a conversion artifact for a Vedic m/anusvāra variant sign); read as ṃ/m

notes: Stray j in 'yajamānaj'. 'vyayantām' governs both 'you' and 'this sacrificer'; 'rāyaḥ' taken as nominative plural. 'viśaḥ' rendered 'clans'.

hindi: तुम समीप जाने वाले हो; देवों के प्रति, दैवी प्रजाओं के प्रति, प्रागु उत्सुकों के प्रति, सबसे अधिक वहन करने वालों के प्रति। हे देव त्वष्टा, धन में रमण करो; तुम्हारे लिए हव्य स्वादिष्ट हों।
english: You are the one who approaches; to the gods, the divine clans, the prāgu eager ones, the best bearers. O god Tvaṣṭṛ, take delight in the good things; may the offerings be sweet to you.
notes: Obscure: 'prāguḥ' (token 'prāgṷru̱śijo̱' read prāguḥ uśijaḥ) is kept untranslated; 'upāvīḥ' glossed 'one who approaches' (doubtful); 'vasu' taken as good things; 'svadantām' as 'be sweet'. The relation of the accusatives to 'asi' is not clear.

hindi: हे धनवती स्त्रियो, रमण करो; हे बृहस्पति, वसुओं को धारण करो। हे देवों के हव्य, मैं तुम्हें ऋत के पाश से बाँधता हूँ। धर्षा, मानुष।
english: O wealthy ones, take delight; O Bṛhaspati, hold the goods. O offering of the gods, I fasten you with the cord of order. Dharṣā, the human.
notes: Obscure: the end 'dharṣā mānuṣaḥ' is left untranslated as 'dharṣā' (form and sense uncertain; possibly an imperative of √dhṛṣ); 'revatīḥ' taken as vocative plural; 'dhārayā' with lengthened final vowel read as an imperative. 'vasūni' rendered 'goods'.

hindi: देव सविता की प्रेरणा में, अश्विनों की भुजाओं से और पूषा के हाथों से, अग्नि और सोम को प्रिय तुम्हें मैं जोड़ता हूँ। जलों के लिए तुम्हें, ओषधियों के लिए तुम्हें। माता अनुमति दे, पिता अनुमति दे, सगा भाई अनुमति दे, एक यूथ का मित्र अनुमति दे। अग्नि और सोम को प्रिय तुम्हें मैं सींचता हूँ।
english: At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the two Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I yoke you, pleasing to Agni and Soma. You for the waters, you for the plants. May the mother consent to you, the father, the brother of the same womb, the friend of the same herd. I sprinkle you, pleasing to Agni and Soma.
notes: 'agnīṣomābhyām juṣṭam' taken as 'pleasing to Agni and Soma' (dative dual form). 'anu ... manyatām' read as 'consent' with 'anu' repeated for each person.

hindi: तुम जलों के पेरु हो। दैवी जल देवों के हव्य को, जो भली-भाँति खाया हुआ है, मधुर करें। तुम्हारा प्राण वायु के साथ मिले, अंग पूजनीयों के साथ मिलें, यज्ञपति आशीष के साथ मिले।
english: You are the peru of the waters. May the divine waters sweeten the well-eaten offering to the gods, which is present. May your breath unite with the wind, your limbs with the worshipful ones, and the lord of the sacrifice with the blessing.

text_flags.why: stray Latin letter j after the word (probably a conversion artifact for a Vedic m/anusvāra variant sign); read as ṃ/m

notes: Obscure: 'peruḥ' left untranslated; 'svāttaṃ cit sad devahaviḥ' taken as 'well-eaten, even being the offering to the gods' (doubtful construction); 'yajatraiḥ' taken as 'worshipful ones' (obscure). 'gacchatāj' contains a stray j.

hindi: घी से अभिषिक्त तुम दोनों पशुओं की रक्षा करो; हे धनवती, यजमान में प्रिय वस्तु रखो, प्रवेश करो। विस्तृत अन्तरिक्ष से, देव वायु के साथ मिलकर, इस हव्य में से स्वयं यज्ञ करो; इसके शरीर के साथ एक हो जाओ। हे वर्ष, बड़े यज्ञ में यज्ञपति को स्थापित करो। स्वाहा देवों के लिए; देवों के लिए स्वाहा।
english: You two, anointed with ghee, protect the animals; O wealthy one, place what is dear in the sacrificer and enter. From the wide atmosphere, in company with the divine wind, sacrifice by yourself of this offering; be one with its body. O varṣa, in the greater sacrifice set the lord of the sacrifice. Svāhā to the gods; to the gods svāhā.

text_flags.why: stray Latin letter j after the word (probably a conversion artifact for a Vedic m/anusvāra variant sign); read as ṃ/m

notes: Obscure: 'varṣaḥ' taken as vocative 'rain' (uncertain) and left as varṣa in the translation; 'varṣīyasi' as 'greater'; 'haviṣaḥ' genitive after 'yaja' read as 'of this offering'. 'trāyethāj' contains a stray j; the dual 'āktau/trāyethām' is as printed. The printed 'devebhyo devebhyaḥ svāhā' repeats 'devebhyaḥ'.

hindi: साँप मत बनो, पृदाकु मत बनो; तुम्हें नमस्कार। हे आतान, बिना बाधा के आगे बढ़ो, घी की धाराओं के साथ-साथ, ऋत के मार्गों के अनुसार।
english: Do not be a snake, do not be a pṛdāku; homage to you. O ātāna, go forth unhindered, along the streams of ghee, along the paths of order.
notes: Obscure: 'ātāna' (taken as a vocative) and 'anarvā' (taken as 'unhindered'); 'pṛdāku' kept as a name of a creature, not identified. 'kulyāḥ' and 'pathyāḥ' read as accusative plurals governed by 'upa' and 'anu'.

hindi: हे दैवी जलो, शुद्ध होकर वहन करो। देवों में भली-भाँति परोसे हुए; भली-भाँति परोसे हुए हम परोसने वाले हों।
english: O divine waters, pure, carry on. Well served among the gods; well served, may we be the servers.

text_flags.why: stray Latin letter j after the word (probably a conversion artifact for a Vedic m/anusvāra variant sign); read as ṃ/m

notes: The construction is uncertain: the two 'supariviṣṭā' are read as 'well served' (the first agreeing with the waters, the second with 'we'); the object of 'voḍhvam' is not stated. 'voḍhvaj' contains a stray j.

hindi: तुम्हारी वाणी को शुद्ध करता हूँ, तुम्हारे प्राण को शुद्ध करता हूँ, तुम्हारी आँख को शुद्ध करता हूँ, तुम्हारे कान को शुद्ध करता हूँ, तुम्हारी नाभि को शुद्ध करता हूँ, तुम्हारे मेढ्र को शुद्ध करता हूँ, तुम्हारी गुदा को शुद्ध करता हूँ, तुम्हारे चरित्रों को शुद्ध करता हूँ।
english: I purify your speech; I purify your breath; I purify your eye; I purify your ear; I purify your navel; I purify your meḍhra; I purify your anus; I purify your means of going.
notes: 'caritrān' (printed 'ca̱ritrā̭~ste') is glossed 'means of going' (commentators take it as feet); 'meḍhra' is kept as the Sanskrit term (the male organ); 'pāyu' rendered 'anus'.

hindi: तुम्हारा मन पूरी तरह पुष्ट हो, तुम्हारी वाणी पुष्ट हो, तुम्हारा प्राण पुष्ट हो, तुम्हारी आँख पुष्ट हो, तुम्हारा कान पुष्ट हो। तुम्हारा जो कठोर है, जो टिका हुआ है, वह पुष्ट हो, हटाया जाए; वह तुम्हारा शुद्ध हो, शुभ दिनों के लिए। हे ओषधि, रक्षा करो; हे स्वधिति, इसे हानि मत पहुँचाओ।
english: May your mind swell fully; may your speech swell fully; may your breath swell fully; may your eye swell fully; may your ear swell fully. What of yours is harsh, what abides, may that swell fully, may it be removed, may that of yours be purified, for happy days. O herb, protect; O blade, do not harm him.

text_flags.why: stray Latin letter j after the word (probably a conversion artifact for a Vedic m/anusvāra variant sign); read as ṃ/m

notes: Obscure: 'niṣṭyāyatām' (sense doubtful) and 'śamahobhyaḥ' (read śam + ahobhyaḥ 'for well-being, for the days'); 'krūram' rendered 'harsh'; 'svadhite' is the vocative of svadhiti, rendered 'blade'. The last token of line 1 'pyāyatāṃj' has a stray j.
